title: Satara District Gazetteer, Volume XIX (History)
author: James M. Campbell, editor; Bombay Presidency Gazetteer series
publisher: Government of Maharashtra, Gazetteer Department (facsimile reprint of 1885 volume; e-book edition 2006)
supports: Identifies the leading Satara-region chiefs under Bijapur: More of Javli, Naik Nimbalkar of Phaltan, Ghatge of Malavdi, Daphle of Jath, Mane of Mhasvad and Ghorpade of Kapshi. Describes the More appointment under Yusuf Adil Shah, Nimbalkar and Bhosle marriage connections, Ghatge deshmukhi and Nagoji's 1626 title, Mane's Mhasvad deshmukhi and Bijapur service, the two Ghorpade lines, Daphle origins/command, and early references to Mohite and Mahadik.
caveat: Retrospective gazetteer, not a contemporary 1622 roster. It mixes early-sixteenth-century narrative with seventeenth-century facts; dates and scope are restricted to what it explicitly states.

title: Shivaji the Maratha: His Life and Times
author: H. G. Rawlinson
supports: Discusses the Bhosle family's early documented status, Lukaji Jadhav Rao of Sindkhed as a Nizam Shahi feudatory, Maloji Bhosle's subordinate service, the 1604 marriage and grant of Poona/Supe jagirs and Chakan/Shivneri forts, Maloji's death in 1619, and Shahaji's return to Ahmadnagar service.
caveat: Early twentieth-century synthesis drawing in part on Bhosle family chronicles; it explicitly treats claimed Chitor descent as an unverified family origin story. Do not turn its anecdotal marriage narrative into a precise genealogical fact beyond what is stated.

title: Shivaji the Founder of Maratha Swaraj
author: C. V. Vaidya
supports: Provides a dated outline of Shahaji's service: Adil Shahi service from about October 1625 to about the end of 1627, with a document dated 10 January 1626 mentioning a desagata and fort rights granted to Sambhaji and Dharoji Mohite; it then describes Shahaji's return to Nizam Shahi service.
caveat: Retrospective monograph. The Mohite connection in this passage is described as probable kinship, not proven parentage; the 1625-1627 service dates are after the 1622 start date.

title: Jedhe, śakāvalī-karīnā (Jedhe Shakavali of Kari)
author: Edited/translated publication associated with A. R. Kulkarni
supports: Identifies the chronicle as preserved by the Jedhes, Deshmukhs of Kari near Bhor, and describes its 1618-1697 coverage. It supports the existence of a Kari Jedhe documentary/household tradition in the relevant period.
caveat: The accessible bibliographic record establishes provenance and coverage, not every individual entry. It does not establish a precise 1622 patron or permit unsupported branch genealogies.

title: Report on the General Administration of the Phaltan State, 1942-43 (including Annex I: Names of the Rulers of the Phaltan State)
author: Government of Phaltan; Dewan's Office
supports: Records the Naik-Nimbalkar house as the ruling house of Phaltan and lists Vangoji II alias Jagpalrao as ruler from 1570 to 1630, placing him in office in 1622.
caveat: A twentieth-century official retrospective chronology; use the named tenure as a dated house chronology, not as proof of every alleged earlier ancestor or exact annual political status.

title: Ghorpade Gharanyacha Itihas (History of the Ghorpade House)
author: B. B. Raje Ghorpade
publisher: Maharashtra Rajya Sahitya ani Sanskruti Mandal, Mumbai
supports: Distinguishes Kapshi and Mudhol Ghorpade houses; identifies the Daphles as Jath deshmukhs with a Chavhan/Daphalapur origin tradition and Bijapur command; describes Shahaji's later 1637 Bijapur service and grant.
caveat: A family history using a family archive. The text itself distinguishes family legend from documented grants; its origin tale that Ghorpades descended from Bhonsles is not treated here as proven kinship.

title: The South Konkan (2): Ports south of Ratnagiri
author: Indian Antiquary contributor; historical passage cites Ferishta as translated by Briggs
publisher: The Indian Antiquary (later digitised by Wisdomlib)
date: Nineteenth-century journal article; passage discusses the 1453 expedition
supports: Describes a Shirke chief in the 1453 Bahmani expedition toward Khelna/Vishalgad and the chief's role in guiding the army through the region.
caveat: This is evidence for a fifteenth-century Shirke chief, not proof of the identity, holdings or patronage of a continuous Shirke branch in 1622.
